pamphlet_excerpts: Public Speaker Predicted: You Are a Public Speaker!
Poking Little Fun: Poking a little fun at yourself is another way to scorepoints with audiences.
Speech Seeks Makethe: The speech seeks to makethe audience believe or accept your point of view, or stimulateor inspire your audience.
Instance Say Live: For instance, let’s say you live in anurban neighborhood.
step_by_step_procedure: City Council Wants: Your city council wants to turn your onlyneighborhood basketball court into a much-needed parking lot.
Decide Speech Class: You decide to give a speech to your class about how much thebasketball court means to you and your friends.
Goal Call Attention: Your goal is to call attention to thisissue and inspire the audience to care about the basketballcourt as much as you do.
Cite Lack Playground: Cite the lack of playground facilities in your area, or how many students who once played at the local courtwent on to play high school and/or.

pamphlet_excerpts: Impromptu Speech Really: An impromptu speech can’t really be compared with a traditionalspeech.
Simply Brief Talk: It is simply a brief talk on a subject the speaker knowssomething about but for which they have had little time to prepare.
Chances Yourself Situation: Chances are, you may find yourself in this situation a coupleof times a week in school.
Suppose Meeting: Suppose you are at a Scout meeting and the Scoutmasterasks you, without warning, to tell the troop about plans foran upcoming campout to Three Rivers State.
step_by_step_procedure: Think Moment Campout: Think for a moment what you know about the campout, then quicklyorganize your thoughts.
Don Afraid Pause: Don’t be afraid to pause for a second and reflect on thequestion or topic you have been asked to present.
Remind End Speech: Remind Scouts at the end of your speech to check with their folks about volunteering as chaperones.
Probablywon Asked Talk: You probablywon’t be asked to talk about a topic you don’t know somethingabout.

pamphlet_excerpts: Now Prepared Speech: Now that you have prepared your speech and practiced infront of friends and family, you are ready to deliver your speech to the intended audience.
Task Prepare Room: Your first task is to prepare the room where you plan to speak.
Equipment Electrical Outlets: If your equipment uses electrical outlets, be prepared!.
Bring Three-prong Two-prong: Bring a three-prong/two-prong outlet adapter and an extensioncord with you.
step_by_step_procedure: Alsobring Small Flashlight: Alsobring a small flashlight or penlight in case you have to darkenthe room and still need to refer to your notes.
Check Seating Arrangement: Check the seating arrangement before anyone arrives.
Expect People Chairs: If you expect 10 people and you have 40 chairs, move 30 ofthem away from the area where you will be speaking.
Arrangesmall-group Seating: Arrangesmall-group seating in a semicircle so that all participants cansee you and one another.

pamphlet_excerpts: Come Order Parliamentary: Come to Order, Parliamentary Procedure Made Easy In formal meetings, the chair, or leader, conducts all business.
Leader Informal Meeting: While the leader of an informal meeting may participatein the discussion, the chair of a formal meeting only conductsthe meeting.
Speakers Recognized Chair: Speakers must be recognized by the chair andtechnically, all remarks are directed to the chair.
Questions from Individual: Questions from individual to individual also are directed via the chair.
step_by_step_procedure: Formal Meeting Debate: The formal meeting is more a debate of opposing ideas, eachof which strives for audience approval.
Chair Enforces Rules: The chair enforces the rules equally on all participants to ensure thateach person has a fair opportunity to present his or her point of view.
Responsibilityfor Themeeting: Responsibilityfor keeping themeeting goingalso meanskeeping itfocused.
Whenthe Discussion Informal: Whenthe discussion While informal discussions do not have rules, the chair mustapply commonsense ideas for a successful meeting to takeplace.
